title: The VGA graphics controller registers
covers: The registers of the VGA graphics controller: the index at port 3CE, the data port 3CF and indices 00 to 09

rows.text: The Address register is at address hex 03CE.
It is loaded with the index value that points to the desired data register within the graphics controller.
The Index field (bits 3-0) contains the index value that points to the data registers.
Bits 7-4 are set to 0.
The upper bits are undefined on read; the figure prints the zero as an OCR e.
The port is reached through write_p3ce and read_p3ce, installed as IO_MB handlers at 0x3CE.
The data registers of the graphics controller are at address hex 03CF.
All registers are read/write.
All registers are read back through address hex 03CF.
At 03CF the registers are 00 Set/Reset, 01 Enable Set/Reset, 02 Color Compare, 03 Data Rotate and 04 Read Map Select.
At 03CF the registers are 05 Graphics Mode, 06 Miscellaneous, 07 Color Don't Care and 08 Bit Mask.
This register has an index of hex 00; its address is hex 03CF.
Bits 3-0 are the Set/Reset fields for maps 3, 2, 1 and 0.
Bits 7-4 are set to 0 and undefined on read; the figure prints the zero as an OCR e.
In write mode 0 the value of each set/reset field is written to its respective memory map.
For each write the set/reset bit, if enabled, is written to all 8 bits within that map.
Set/reset can be enabled on a map-by-map basis through the Enable Set/Reset register.
The handler precomputes each field's whole-plane value and the enabled set/reset combination.

rows.text: The index of this register is hex 01; its address is hex 03CF.
Bits 3-0 are the Enable Set/Reset fields for maps 3, 2, 1 and 0.
Bits 7-4 are set to 0 and undefined on read; the figure prints the zero as an OCR e.
These fields enable the set/reset function used when write mode 0 is selected.
When set to 1, the respective memory map receives the value in the Set/Reset register.
When set/reset is not enabled for a map, that map receives the value sent by the system.
The handler expands the enable field into a whole-plane value and keeps its complement.

rows.text: This register has an index of hex 02; its address is hex 03CF.
CC3-CC0 (bits 3-0) make up the 4-bit color value compared in read mode 1.
Bits 7-4 are set to 0 and undefined on read; the figure prints the zero as an OCR e.
In read mode 1 a memory read returns a 1 in each bit position where the four maps equal the Color Compare register.
If the read mode bit is 0, the data is returned without comparison.
The 8 bit positions are compared across the four maps, and a 1 is returned where the bits of all four maps equal their color compare values.
The handler also keeps a copy of the field in the VGA configuration.
This register has an index of hex 03; its address is hex 03CF.
FS (bits 4-3) is the Function Select field and RC (bits 2-0) the Rotate Count field.
Bits 7-5 are set to 0 and undefined on read; the figure prints the zero as an OCR a.
The Function Select field determines whether and how data written to the buffer is operated on with the system latches.
The logical operations selected are data unmodified, ANDed, ORed or XORed with the latched data.
In write mode 0 the Rotate Count selects the positions the system data is rotated right during a memory write.
Data can be any of the choices selected by the write mode bits except the system latches, and a rotate is performed before the logical operation.
The handler also records, as complexity, whether a rotate count or a raster operation is active.

rows.text: This register has an index of hex 04; its address is hex 03CF.
The Map Select field (bits 1-0) is named MS.
Bits 7-2 are set to 0 and undefined on read.
The Map Select field selects the memory map for system read operations and has no effect on the color compare read mode.
In odd/even modes, 00 or 01 selects the chained maps 0 and 1, and 10 or 11 the chained maps 2 and 3.
This register has an index of hex 05; its address is hex 03CF.
Bit 6 is C256, bit 5 SR, bit 4 OE, bit 3 RM and bits 1-0 WM.
Bits 7 and 2 are set to 0 and undefined on read.
C256 set to 1 causes the shift registers to be loaded in a manner that supports the 256-color mode.
SR set to 1 formats the serial data stream with even bits on even maps and odd bits on odd maps.
OE set to 1 selects the odd/even addressing mode, normally following sequencer Memory Mode register bit 2.
DOSBox-X takes odd/even addressing from bit 1 of the Miscellaneous register; the handler stores this whole byte and the memory path tests only that bit.
When RM is 1, reads return the comparison of the four maps and the Color Compare register.
When RM is 0, data is read from the memory map selected by the Read Map Select register.
The map may instead be selected by the 2 low-order bits of the memory address, depending on the chain-4 bit.
WM selects the write mode; the function select logic applies to modes 0, 2 and 3.
Mode 0 writes each map with the system data rotated by the Data Rotate count, or with the Set/Reset value where enabled.
Mode 1 writes each map with the contents of the system latches, which a read loads.
Mode 2 fills memory map n (0 through 3) with the value of data bit n; the figure's count of bits is an OCR glyph.
Mode 3 writes each map with its Set/Reset value and uses rotated data ANDed with the Bit Mask.
The handler re-determines the video mode and the memory handlers when the upper bits change.
The drawing path reads bit 5 of this register to choose the 2BPP line drawer.

rows.text: This register has an index of hex 06; its address is hex 03CF.
Bits 3-2 are MM Memory Map, bit 1 is OE and bit 0 is GM.
Bits 7-4 are set to 0 and undefined on read; the figure prints the zero as an OCR e.
MM controls the mapping of the regenerative buffer into the system address space, as A0000 128KB, A0000 64KB, B0000 32KB or B8000 32KB.
OE set to 1 replaces address bit A0 with a higher-order bit, selecting the odd map when A0 is 1 and the even map when A0 is 0.
GM set to 1 selects graphics mode addressing and disables the character generator latches.
The handler stores the whole byte and re-determines the mode and the memory handlers when the Memory Map bits change; the case never reads GM bit 0.
The handler stores the byte and re-determines the video mode and the memory handlers when MM changes.
This register has an index of hex 07; its address is hex 03CF.
M3X-M0X (bits 3-0) are the map don't care fields.
Bits 7-4 are set to 0 and undefined on read; the figure prints the zero as an OCR a.
The fields select whether a map participates in the color compare cycle.
When set to 1, the bits in that map are compared.
The handler also keeps a copy of the field in the VGA configuration, for the read comparison.
This register has an index of hex 08; its address is hex 03CF.
The register holds a Bit Mask in bits 7-0.
A bit set to 1 lets the corresponding bit position in each map change; a bit set to 0 masks it, if the location was the last one read.
The bit mask applies to write mode 0.
The bit mask applies to write mode 2.
To preserve bits using the bit mask, data must be latched internally by reading the location.
When data is written to preserve the bits, the most current data in the latches is written in those positions.
The bit mask applies to all maps simultaneously.
Unusual use of the bit mask in chained 256-color mode switches the handler to a slower, accurate path.

rows.text: Index 9 is not among the registers 0-8 the data port decodes, so its accesses reach the default branch, where the SVGA handler receives them.
When an SVGA write handler exists it receives the index and the value.
With no SVGA handler the first write to index 9 logs an illegal index 9 warning and later writes log the generic illegal index warning.
The read handler's default branch passes the index to the SVGA read handler when one exists, and otherwise logs and returns 0.
